To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a coherence based separable likelihood model for feature correspondences can be computed from noisy matches; 2) this model can be used to filter the set of all matches for true matches, even over large baselines; 3) this model can also be used to filter matches for a given set of correspondences, thus improving the quality of the final set of matches.

(1) Coherence based decision boundaries can be discovered from noisy matches; (2) The decision boundaries can be used to filter out false matches and generate large numbers of high quality correspondences; (3) The technique can be applied to any feature descriptor and can be combined with other correspondence techniques.

(1) the coherence of true matches and randomness of false matches can be used to filter out most of the false matches; (2) this can be done by learning a correspondence likelihood model from a few noisy matches and (3) the resulting correspondence likelihood model can be used for filtering the entire set of candidate matches.
